content.text: `alinea/sveltekit` connects Alinea to SvelteKit with a `handle` hook. Your site serves the dashboard and the Alinea API, and the queries in your server load functions see drafts while an editor previews a page. It runs on Node, for example with `@sveltejs/adapter-node`.
Install
Create the CMS

The Alinea CLI looks for your config in `cms.ts` or `src/cms.ts`, so create `src/cms.ts` rather than a file in `src/lib` (or point the CLI to it with `--config`). Import `createCMS` from `alinea/server`. SvelteKit serves static files from the `static` folder, so set `publicDir` and keep media there. `vite dev` listens on port 5173:
The CMS reads its content database with Node APIs, so only import `cms.ts` in server code: `hooks.server.ts`, `+page.server.ts`, `+layout.server.ts` and `+server.ts` files.
Add the handle hook
`createHandle(cms)` returns a SvelteKit `handle` hook. Export it from `src/hooks.server.ts`:

The hook answers the Alinea API on `/api/cms`, media files under `/admin/file/` and the dashboard on `/admin`. Every other request resolves within it, so queries see drafts when an editor previews the page. Combine it with your own hooks using `sequence`, with Alinea first:
`createHandle` takes the same options as the
middleware for Node servers
, such as a custom backend, commit hooks and the previews.
Query content
Query the CMS in server load functions and `+server.ts` endpoints. They run within the request, so editors previewing the page see its drafts:
Universal load functions in `+page.ts` and `+layout.ts` also run in the browser, where the CMS is not available. Query in `+page.server.ts` or `+layout.server.ts` and return the data your page needs.
Develop and build
Run Vite through the Alinea CLI. It generates your content database, starts the dashboard and passes its location to your site in environment variables:

Open `http://localhost:5173/admin` to edit content: during development the hook proxies the dashboard to the Alinea CLI. `alinea build` writes the production dashboard into `static/admin.html` and `static/admin/` before Vite builds your site, so add both to your `.gitignore`.
Live previews

The dashboard previews an entry by loading its page with a preview token, which the hook turns into a draft cookie. Draft pages get a small script that receives the edits from the dashboard and reloads the page. To update the page in place instead, rerun its load functions with `invalidateAll` in `src/hooks.client.ts`:

Each edit then updates the page without losing its scroll position or component state, also after the editor navigated to another page within the preview. With `previews: {widget: true}` draft pages also show the floating preview toolbar.
Prerendering

Pages with `export const prerender = true` render during `vite build`, from the content database the Alinea CLI generated just before. They contain the content published at build time, so rebuild your site to update them. Prerendered pages are static files: they show no drafts or live previews, so keep the pages editors preview dynamic.
Deploy

Your site needs a Node runtime, such as `@sveltejs/adapter-node`: pages query the SQLite database generated in `@alinea/generated`, so deploy `node_modules` with your build. Edge runtimes are not supported.
Set `ALINEA_API_KEY` in the production environment. The handler uses it to sign preview tokens and draft cookies, and to talk to its backend.
With `adapter-node`, set `ORIGIN` to the URL of your site. SvelteKit otherwise assumes `https`, which breaks preview redirects on plain `http`.
The handler saves edits as commits through
Alinea Cloud or your own backend
. Running servers sync their database with the handler, so published changes show without a redeploy.
